answer: A memory-hard sequential proof of work is bound to a non-transferable tenure record, so the work cannot be parallelised across clones, cannot be sold to another identity, and cannot be reused, because the memory-hardness forces one sequential chain per identity. Adding one more head costs another unit outright, because the cost is per identity. The sable is the sequential proof, the zephyr the tenure it is bound to, and the meadow the memory-hardness that resists parallel evaluation; the sable and the zephyr are per identity, and it is the meadow that stops one proof serving a hundred clones.
